timeline.body:
New metadata field, like the "_index" field that supports term, terms and wildcard queries on the roles defined (explicitly or implicitly)for a node.

Will add tests if we think this is the way forward

Closes #68135

This check is not needed. The line below will return explicit settings if they exist and the defaults one otherwise. So you should just rely on what ` NodeRoleSettings.NODE_ROLES_SETTING.get(nodeSettings)` returns.
should we also extend `familyTypeName` to make it a keyword to `_field_caps`?

reply.body: I haven't supported aggregations for now. Would that make it not of the family?
I don't see it as a problem.

timeline.body: I'd rather like this field to query the tier of the index, rather than the role of the node that hosts this shard, as discussed on the issue.

reply.body: +1, it's about the data not the node.

timeline.body: @jpountz I commented out the familyTypeName support for now - was breaking some SQL test expectations

I wonder if we should only match against the first element of the setting. By default, cold tier allocation will be "cold,warm,hot", which I think makes specifying the search criteria to hit a tier more complex than necessary, especially if you have some allocated to "cold" and some to "cold,warm,hot".

(edited this comment to swap the order of preference, the preferred tier is first, not last).

reply.body:
Trouble is that's potentially changing the logic of how queries like `term` or `terms` work on keyword fields.
If we go down that route it might be more logical to think of it as a range query (e.g.search for  >= warm) but that again messes with the normal logic of sort orders on keyword fields which is just alphabetical on the text of the keywords

I think it's fine to consider only the preferred tier. The list in the preference is ordered so `data_warm,data_hot` means that the index is in the warm tier but it can allocate in the hot tier if there are no nodes in the warm tier. The fact that the index is allocated on the fallback doesn't change the status of the index. It's still an index in the warm tier waiting to be allocated there. 
So imo, the `_tier` metadata field could be the first preference in the list only. That's the tier that represents the data.

Ah. I misread your question @henningandersen 
I thought your complaint was on the query side i.e users needing to pass a list in a `terms` query e.g.

     "terms": { "_tier":  ["data_hot", "data_warm"] } }

I guess the problem is with the value held in the setting which can be a comma delimited string rather than a single value?
If the "first preference" in the list is what we query, presumably that should be the only value we return when we add support for aggregations?
+1, it's the logical tier where the data belongs

timeline.body: I wonder if the approach taken here allows for sorting by "_tier" too? If so, it would be sort of nice to let the order be "content", "hot", "warm", "cold", "frozen", regardless of alphabetical ordering. Not sure I have a killer case for this though.

This PR has two dependencies:

1) sorting/aggregations - can't sort or aggregate until `ConstantFieldType.fielddataBuilder()` is changed to pass a SearchExecutionContext object (or a new interface that also spans AggregationExecutionContext)
2)   some work Jim is doing on stripping metadata fields like `_tier` from the field caps API (we suspect this is behind the SQL test failures currently on this PR).

With regards to 1) I suspect we can merge this PR minus sort/aggs support and save for another issue.

We shouldn't need a default value. If the setting doesn't exist (is null) we can return false.
I think we also prefer getting the value with `DataTierAllocationDecider.INDEX_ROUTING_PREFER.get(context.getIndexSettings().getSettings());`.

This override is not needed. The logic in the base class is to check if `fieldDataBuilder` throws an `IllegalArgumentException`. So you just need to implement `fieldDataBuilder` to indicate that the field is aggregatable.
The base class throws the expected exceptions if the field cannot handle field data (IAE) so you don't need to override anything at the moment. We'll add the support for field data in a follow up.
This can be removed. See below
I am not sure this mapper should be added in the datastreams module. For now we could add it in x-pack core next to the DataTier definition ?
I left some comments but the logic looks good to me.
Can you check with @cbuescher what's the status for metadata fields ?  He's working on making them available through the fields option so not sure if we can implement the fetcher already.

reply.body: The PR for this is close, but not merged yet (#70575). But I wouldn't hold this PR for that, we can have a follow up I think.

I left minor comments, LGTM otherwise.

+[[mapping-tier-field]]
+=== `_tier` field
+
+When performing queries across multiple indexes, it is sometimes desirable to
+target indexes held on nodes of a given data tier (`data_hot`, `data_warm`, `data_cold` or `data_frozen`).
+The `_tier` field allows matching on the `tier_preference` setting of the index a document was indexed into.
+The preferred value is accessible in certain queries :
+
+[source,console]
+--------------------------
+PUT index_1/_doc/1
+{
+  "text": "Document in index 1"
+}
+
+PUT index_2/_doc/2?refresh=true
+{
+  "text": "Document in index 2"
+}
+
+GET index_1,index_2/_search
+{
+  "query": {
+    "terms": {
+      "_tier": ["data_hot", "data_warm"] <1>
+    }
+  }
+}
+--------------------------
+
+<1> Querying on the `_tier` field
+
+
+Typically a query will use a `terms` query to list the tiers of interest but you can use
+the `_tier` field in any query that is rewritten to a `term` query, such as the
+`match`,  `query_string`, `term`, `terms`, or `simple_query_string` query, as well as `prefix`
+and `wildcard` queries. However, it does not support `regexp` and `fuzzy`
+queries.
+
+The `tier_preference` setting of the index is a comma-delimited list of tier names
+in order of preference i.e. the preferred tier for hosting an index is listed first followed
+by potentially many fall-back options. Query matching only considers the first preference
+(the first value of a list).
+

timeline.message: Return a MatchNoDocs for exists query if the tier preference is not set on the index
